angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 278,280 km at 171.46 pc = 0.02 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.8323 +/- 0.0274 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 171.46 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.4 +/- 0.01 solar radii from Cañas et al. 2022, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of KOI-4777.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163....3C/abstract): 278,280 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.41 +/- 0.02 solar masses from Cañas et al. 2022, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of KOI-4777.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163....3C/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3515 +/- 69 K from Cañas et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KOI-4777.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163....3C/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Cañas et al. 2022, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of KOI-4777.01 in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2022AJ....163....3C/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/koi-4777.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.847, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
